title: Organise messages and work through a list
outcome: Find the open messages belonging to one member of the team.
story: A count alone cannot tell Amina who should answer each message. The shop needs a list of messages with an identifier, a status, and an owner.

demo.title: Find the work left to do

frames.explanation: A filter keeps items that meet a condition.
Another condition can choose work belonging to one person.

sections.title: One message has several details
paragraphs: An object groups named details about one thing. A message might be { id: 1, status: "open", owner: "Amina" }. We use message.status to read its status, just as we use a label to find a value.
An identifier is a value used to recognise an item. Two messages can have the same text, so their text is a poor identifier. A stable id lets the interface update the intended message.

sections.title: An array holds a list
paragraphs: An array is an ordered list of values. Our inbox is an array of message objects. An empty inbox is [], a valid array with no items. It should produce an empty result rather than an error.
A new array can hold the identifiers we want to return. We start with let openIds = [] and add a matching id with openIds.push(message.id). The original inbox stays available for other operations.

sections.title: Repeat a rule for each item
paragraphs: A loop repeats instructions. for (const message of messages) visits each message in the list. Inside the loop, an if condition decides whether to include that message.

We want an open status and, when an owner is selected, the matching owner. The symbol && means both conditions must be true. The symbol || means either condition can be true. An empty owner selection means show all open messages.

sections.title: Choose data carefully
paragraphs: Filtering is useful for views, reports, and search. Amina can see her open work without deleting other messages. A filter should preserve the identifiers and ordering of the selected items.

A browser filter is not permission enforcement. Later, the backend will check who is allowed to read each record. For this exercise, all records are authorised fictional data and we are choosing the useful view.

words.meaning: Named details grouped together for one item.
Instructions repeated for each item or until a condition changes.

explanation: The array contains two message objects.
The loop visits both objects. === compares values without changing them.
Only the open message contributes its id to the result.

exercise.title: Build a useful inbox view
exercise.brief: Return the ids of open messages. When owner is an empty string, show all open messages. Otherwise, show only that owner’s open messages.

steps.title: Read each identifier
steps.task: Visit each message and add its id to openIds. Start with a queue containing only open messages.
steps.hint: Use for (const message of messages) and openIds.push(message.id).
steps.solution:
let openIds = [];
for (const message of messages) { openIds.push(message.id); }

steps.title: Keep only open messages
steps.task: Add a status condition so closed messages are excluded.

steps.title: Respect the owner selection
steps.task: Keep all open messages when owner is "". For a named owner, return only that person’s open messages.
steps.hint: The owner condition is owner === "" || message.owner === owner. Combine it with the status condition using &&.

cases.label: Two open messages
cases.why: Read every matching item, not just the first.

cases.label: An empty inbox
cases.why: No work should give an empty list.

cases.label: Open and closed messages
cases.why: Closed work does not belong in the open view.

cases.label: No open work
cases.why: A non-empty source can still have no matches.

cases.label: Amina’s open work
cases.why: Both status and owner must match.

cases.label: An owner with no messages
cases.why: An unknown selection must not reveal another person’s items.

project.title: A team inbox filter
project.brief: Give Amina a view of unfinished messages, with a choice of owner. Use fictional records and stable identifiers.
deliverables: An array of at least six message objects.
A filter that returns matching ids.
Examples covering empty and mixed queues.

milestones.title: Describe the data
actions: Give each message an id, status, and owner.

milestones.title: Check the view
actions: Record results for all owners and one named owner.
Confirm the original records are still intact.

acceptance: A named owner excludes other owners.
An empty owner selection includes all open work.
The original data and identifier order are preserved.

tests.situation: Open messages owned by Amina and Bilal; select Amina

project.extension: Add a count of matching messages alongside the ids. Do not confuse a view filter with server-side permissions.
reflection: Why use an id rather than message text?
What does the loop do for an empty array?
What would a backend still need to check?
